links.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM answer accuracy across user accounts and seven consecutive days
links.effect: No account-related variability (p = 0.654) and no temporal drift (p = 0.875); overall accuracy 90.8%.
links.quote: Accuracy remained stable across user accounts and evaluation days, with no evidence of account-related variability (p = 0.654) or temporal drift (p = 0.875).

links.outcome: Error rates of document-grounded (RAG) versus base LLM configurations on ECR questions
links.effect: Configuration affected performance (p = 0.050); NotebookLM (RAG) 3.0% and Gemini (Base) 4.0% lowest error; Claude (Base) highest at 12.0%.
links.quote: Model configuration significantly influenced performance (p = 0.050), with NotebookLM and Gemini showing the lowest estimated error rates (3.0% and 4.0%, respectively), while Claude demonstrated the highest error rate (12.0%).

screen.reason: The study compares baseline LLMs against document-grounded (RAG) configurations across multiple days to evaluate accuracy, consistency, and temporal drift on clinical dental questions.
